metadata.title: The Cheaply Built Dam That Swept Away Four Villages
metadata.description:
Mill River failed and flooded four Massachusetts villages. The cause: failure of an earthen dam built with cost-cutting changes to its core wall.

Failure chain: Design changed to save money → Weak core wall → Seepage → Embankment slides → Flood sweeps valley

Related episode: The Flood That Proved Levees Alone Couldn't Hold the Mississippi — https://youtu.be/UOGvy9hscUM

Series — Infrastructure Failures: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLEtVY8dbosy0

Technical references:
• Wikipedia — Mill River Flood of 1874 — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mill_River_Flood_of_1874
• USGS — report (cited by Wikipedia) — https://pubs.usgs.gov/wsp/0798/report.pdf

Narration uses a synthetic voice. Original animation: no archival or stock footage; reconstructions and illustrations are labelled on screen.
